title: About the Foundation
text: About the Foundation - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content About the Foundation Strong Starts. Lasting Results. The Wexmoor Foundation invests in public education, with a clear focus on early grades achievement and on excellent educators and school leaders , the two foundations on which every student's success is built. As a private family foundation, we look for partners who share our sense of urgency. Our support goes beyond dollars: we give our time, our voice and our convening power. We learn by listening to the people closest to students'teachers whose classrooms consistently outperform expectations, principals who have turned schools around, and leaders of organizations that are meeting ambitious goals. We build relationships with high-performing organizations and results-focused school systems because we believe that, working together, we can help every child read, learn and lead. Our Commitment to Equity and Belonging As a foundation dedicated to an excellent public education for every student, The Wexmoor Foundation is committed to equity in how we learn, how we work and where we invest. You can read more about how we reflect, learn and improve here . From the Board Chair Our History Our Approach Our People Financials In the News 2026 Annual Report The Wexmoor Foundation invests around $2.4 million each year to strengthen public education.

title: From the Board Chair
text: From the Board Chair - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content From the Board Chair I have always believed that a great public school can change the direction of a young person's life. North Carolina has a proud tradition of public education, and yet too many of our children still leave third grade unable to read well, and too many classrooms still struggle to attract and keep excellent teachers. Through our two focus areas, early grades achievement and excellent educators and leaders , we at The Wexmoor Foundation see real opportunities to create lasting change for students in Brannock County and across our state. Teachers and principals are the most important in-school factors in how much students learn. We support efforts to recruit, prepare, develop and keep the very best educators in our schools. We also know that a strong early foundation makes every later year easier. Alongside programs that work directly with children, we support efforts to improve early literacy systems and the state policies that shape kindergarten through third grade classrooms. The Wexmoor Foundation's story began in 1931 with my great-grandfather, Ambrose Wexmoor, and his brother, Silas, and it has been carried forward by four generations of our family. We are deeply committed to our mission, and we know we do not have every answer. We are always learning and always looking for new partners. We hope you will join us in working toward an excellent public education for every child. Margaret Wexmoor Ellison, Board Chair of The Wexmoor Foundation

title: Our Approach
text: Our Approach - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Our Approach Our Commitment to Equity and Belonging As a foundation dedicated to an excellent public education for every student, The Wexmoor Foundation is committed to equity in how we learn, how we work and where we invest. You can read more about how we reflect, learn and improve here . Our Board of Directors adopted our Beliefs to Action for two reasons: to set clear standards for our own practice, and to hold ourselves accountable to them. We want our actions to match our words in every interaction with our community. We feel a deep responsibility to our grantee partners and to the philanthropic legacy of our founders. Beliefs to Action: What We Believe, and How We Act on It EVERY CHILD CAN ACHIEVE - We believe every child can achieve at high levels, which is why gaps in achievement between students from low-income families and their more affluent peers are unacceptable and must be closed. - Our community is stronger when every student has fair access to excellent teachers and leaders, to resources, and to the supports that help children learn. - Strong foundational skills in the early grades make later learning possible and reduce the need for costly remediation. How we work to achieve this: ' We focus our resources on the students who need them most, most often students from low-income families. ' When we invest in improving systems, we ask who benefits and who is left out. Strong systems meet the needs of every child. ' We favor prevention and lasting structural improvement over repair. LEADERSHIP MATTERS - Leaders shape the culture and results of every organization, system, school and classroom. - Principals set high expectations and build teams of educators who can meet them. - Every educator, from first-year teacher to district leader, benefits from coaching, reliable data, time to reflect and real chances to grow. - Teachers and leaders should be well supported and should share responsibility for student learning. How we work to achieve this: ' We look for partnerships that strengthen the connected parts of a talent system. ' We weigh the track record and effectiveness of the leadership team, from senior staff to the board. ' We expect clear evidence of leadership commitment before we invest. RESULTS GUIDE US - Measurement and evidence tell us whether organizations, programs and, ultimately, students are making progress. - Curriculum and instruction should be grounded in evidence and research. - Strong schools and districts should have room to innovate, together with accountability for results. - Proficiency is a central goal for every student, and growth is an essential measure of progress along the way. How we work to achieve this: ' We prioritize investments built on evidence-based strategies. ' We support partners who measure their work through both qualitative and quantitative data and use what they learn to improve. ' We treat evaluation as a tool for learning, not only for compliance. BETTER TOGETHER - We keep students at the center and value transparency, accountability, continuous learning and partnership. - Public schools are a cornerstone of our communities, and public dollars carry a responsibility for openness and results. - No single organization has every answer; partnership and shared learning produce the best results. How we work to achieve this: ' Beyond funding, we aim to be a connector and an advocate for positive and lasting change. ' We try to model the partnership, learning and accountability we hope to see in our grantees. ' We pair investments in system improvement with partnerships that reach students directly every day.

title: Our History
text: Our History - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Our History A Tradition of Giving For more than ninety years, the Wexmoor family has supported schools, congregations, hospitals and civic organizations in the North Carolina Piedmont. Based in Harlow Springs, The Wexmoor Foundation carries forward the commitment to community begun by brothers Ambrose and Silas Wexmoor, who founded the Wexmoor Furniture Company in 1909. The Ambrose Wexmoor Memorial Fund was established by the company in 1931 following Ambrose Wexmoor's death. The fund first helped rebuild schoolhouses and libraries in the mill villages around Harlow Springs, and over time it supported a wide range of health, education and community causes. In 1957, after the death of Silas Wexmoor, his heirs joined the charitable portion of his estate with the Memorial Fund to create The Wexmoor Foundation. Today the Foundation remains a family foundation that looks to its founders for inspiration and seeks to express the family's values through its charitable investments. Mr. Wexmoor knew the name of every person on the factory floor and the names of their children. He used to say that a town is only as strong as its schools, and he meant it. For many years, the Wexmoor Furniture Company made annual contributions to the Foundation in support of its charitable work. The company was sold in 2015, and the Foundation has always operated as a separate entity, rooted in the same family history of care for the people of the Piedmont. In 2011, the Board of Directors adopted a new mission statement that placed public education at the center of the Foundation's work. To deepen the impact of its giving, the Foundation now invests only in programs within its two focus areas: early grades achievement and excellent educators and leaders.

title: Brannock County Schools Expands Literacy Coaching Network
text: Brannock County Schools Expands Literacy Coaching Network - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Brannock County Schools Expands Literacy Coaching Network February 20, 2025 Brannock County Schools announced that every elementary school in the district will have access to a trained literacy coach beginning in the 2025-26 school year. The expansion builds on a three-year pilot supported by the Brannock County Schools Education Fund and the Brannock Coaching Collaborative. Coaches work alongside kindergarten through third grade teachers on foundational reading instruction and on using screening data to plan small-group lessons. title: Become Our Partner
text: Become Our Partner - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Become Our Partner Illustration: Wexmoor Foundation The Wexmoor Foundation invests more than dollars. We invest our time, our voice and our energy. We pursue our mission hands-on, spending time in schools and communities and asking good questions of the people who know what works: teachers whose students thrive, principals who have beaten the odds, and leaders of organizations that are exceeding their goals. We are always looking for organizations that share our passion, our goals and our commitment. The Foundation conducts two grantmaking cycles each year, one in the spring and one in the fall, and final applications are by invitation only. Our process is clear and consistent because, above all, we want to respect your time. We believe we can help bring about lasting change. We believe that our work, joined with the work of like-minded partners, can set every student on a path to success. And we are confident that the progress we make now will help build a future in which every child has access to an excellent education and to passionate, skilled teachers and leaders. title: FAQs
text: FAQs - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content FAQs Can I get a scholarship for my child? We do not make grants to individuals. The Wexmoor Foundation has endowed scholarship funds at several North Carolina colleges and universities, but it is not able to award scholarships to individual students. Does The Wexmoor Foundation make grants outside the United States? No. The Wexmoor Foundation makes grants only within the United States. Do you have application deadlines? Yes. Our spring application deadline is in February and our fall application deadline is in August; however, the Foundation accepts applications only from organizations it has invited to apply. Please review our Application Process . How do I get an application? The Wexmoor Foundation awards most of its grants to organizations identified by our staff and board. Please review our Application Process to learn how to introduce your organization to the Foundation. Can we apply if we are not a nonprofit organization? Only nonprofit organizations, public school districts, private schools, and colleges and universities may apply for funding. Can we apply through our fiscal sponsor? In some circumstances you may apply through a fiscal sponsor. The fiscal sponsor must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with a formal relationship to the organization carrying out the project. In these cases the grant is made directly to the fiscal sponsor, which is responsible for the proper use of funds and for all reporting requirements. What is the relationship between The Wexmoor Foundation and the Silas Wexmoor Trust? The Silas Wexmoor Trust is a separate private foundation that supports workforce training and community college pathways for adult learners. It was established in 1988 by Silas Wexmoor Jr. and has its own board, staff and grantmaking process. What is the relationship between The Wexmoor Foundation and Wexmoor Furniture Company? The Wexmoor Foundation is a family foundation established by the founders of the Wexmoor Furniture Company. The Foundation has always been a separate entity from the company, which was sold in 2015 and has no role in the Foundation's governance or grantmaking. Does the Foundation sponsor events? No, the Foundation does not sponsor fundraising events. Can I request items for a raffle or silent auction? The Wexmoor Foundation does not provide merchandise or donated items. Does the Foundation have a limit to Indirect (or F&A) Costs? It is the policy of The Wexmoor Foundation Board of Directors to allow up to 12% of a grant to an institution of higher education to be used for indirect overhead expenses, or 'F&A.' A copy of this policy can be found here .

title: Grant Application Process
text: Grant Application Process - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Grant Application Process Step 1: Determine your fit and take Eligibility Quiz We partner with nonprofit organizations holding 501(c)(3) status, and we also make direct grants to public school districts, to private schools, and to colleges and universities. Our resources are dedicated to Early Grades Achievement and Educators & Leaders , locally in Brannock County and at the state level across North Carolina. To judge whether your organization is a strong fit, we encourage you to review the following: Our approach Our guidelines Outcomes sought Past grantees If, after reviewing these materials, you see clear alignment between your organization's work and our mission, please complete the Foundation's Eligibility Quiz . Step 2: Submit a Letter of Inquiry Organizations that meet the basic requirements in the Eligibility Quiz will be taken to a Letter of Inquiry form, which asks for: Contact information Organization's federal Tax ID (EIN) A short description of how your organization's purpose and/or program advances the mission of the Foundation Geographic area served Within a few weeks of receiving your inquiry, we will let you know whether your organization or program appears to align with the Foundation's desired outcomes . Please note that an initial expression of interest does not guarantee that your organization will be invited to apply for funding. Step 3: Submit a Grant Application (by invitation only) If your organization is selected to submit a full application, a member of the Foundation staff will contact you. Because we are focused on results, our application asks you to describe the specific results your organization commits to achieving and the evidence you will use to measure progress. Please refer to our Outcomes Sought document as you prepare the final application, particularly when describing how you will measure success. The Foundation conducts two grantmaking cycles each year'one in the spring and one in the fall. Spring cycle applications are issued in January, and fall cycle applications are issued in July. Step 4: Proposal Review & Funding Determination Final applications are reviewed by the Grants Committee and then presented to the Board of Directors for approval. The Board meets in April and in October/November to make final funding decisions. Foundation staff will notify applicants once funding decisions have been confirmed.

title: Our Commitment to Equity and Belonging
text: Our Commitment to Equity and Belonging - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Our Commitment to Equity and Belonging As a foundation dedicated to an excellent public education for every student, The Wexmoor Foundation is committed to making sure that our learning and our actions reflect equity and belonging. This commitment makes our work more relevant, more credible and more effective, and it strengthens our ability to fulfill our mission. We seek out a wide range of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences among the people we listen to, learn from and invest in. We work toward policies and practices that give children of every background a genuine opportunity to thrive, and we strive to create an environment where our staff, board, volunteers and partners are respected and heard. This is ongoing work. Each year the Board and staff review how our grantmaking, our convenings and our own operations reflect these commitments, and we share what we learn in our annual report .

title: Read Brannock Marks Ten Years of Community Literacy Work
text: Read Brannock Marks Ten Years of Community Literacy Work - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Read Brannock Marks Ten Years of Community Literacy Work March 4, 2026 Ten years after The Wexmoor Foundation convened community leaders around a simple question, how many of our third graders can read, Read Brannock has grown into a county-wide network of schools, libraries, families and volunteers. The anniversary celebration at the Harlow Springs Public Library recognized the teachers, tutors and family literacy partners who carry the work forward each day. Executive Director Dr. Renee Callahan noted that the Foundation remains a committed lead funder of Read Brannock's operations. Read Brannock will release an updated community literacy scorecard later this spring. Posted in In the News ' Previous: The Wexmoor Foundation Statement on Teacher Residency Pathways

text: Dr. Renee Callahan Named Executive Director of The Wexmoor Foundation - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Dr. Renee Callahan Named Executive Director of The Wexmoor Foundation July 12, 2023 The Wexmoor Foundation Board of Directors announced the selection of Dr. Renee Callahan as the Foundation's next Executive Director, following a national search. title: The Wexmoor Foundation Statement on Teacher Residency Pathways
text: The Wexmoor Foundation Statement on Teacher Residency Pathways - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content The Wexmoor Foundation Statement on Teacher Residency Pathways November 18, 2025 The Wexmoor Foundation shares a few reflections on its support of teacher residency pathways across North Carolina and what we have learned from partners preparing new teachers for high-need classrooms. We believe that beginning teachers deserve a full year of practice alongside an excellent mentor teacher before leading a classroom of their own. Residency programs that pair rigorous coursework with that kind of clinical experience are showing promising early results in retention and classroom readiness. We will continue to learn alongside our partners and share what we learn with the field. title: What We Fund
text: What We Fund - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content What We Fund The Wexmoor Foundation invests in public education, and we are committed to supporting programs that deliver measurable results for students in North Carolina. Our two focus areas, early grades achievement and excellent educators and leaders , are among the most reliable ways to set children on a path to success. We are always looking for partners who share our goals and for programs that advance our mission. Mission & Guidelines Early Grades Achievement Educators & Leaders Our Grantees Children who read on grade level by the end of third grade are far more likely to finish high school, and no school factor matters more to their learning than an excellent teacher.

title: Early Grades Achievement
text: Early Grades Achievement - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Early Grades Achievement Illustration: Wexmoor Foundation The years from kindergarten through third grade are when children learn to read. Every year after that, they read to learn. A strong early foundation is essential to future success in school. During the formative years from kindergarten through third grade, children build the foundational skills, and the love of learning, that carry them through school. Within our Early Grades Achievement focus area, we look for partners who help students perform on or above grade level in core subjects by the end of third grade, starting in kindergarten. Outcomes Sought We support organizations that measure their results and use evidence-based strategies. In Early Grades Achievement, we pay particular attention to student growth as well as improved test scores. Our Outcomes Sought document summarizes our priorities and serves as a basis for conversation with grantees. We welcome a dialogue with grantseekers about their approach and how they use data. Strategic Issue: Early Reading Proficiency Illustration: Wexmoor Foundation In Brannock County, the Foundation's goal, in partnership with Read Brannock, is to increase the percentage of third graders reading at College and Career Ready levels on the state reading assessment from 31% in spring 2023 to 75% by spring 2031. Alongside our local strategy, at the North Carolina state level, the Foundation supports research, policy and effective practice to raise third grade reading proficiency. A particular priority is making sure every elementary teacher has the knowledge and skill to teach reading to every learner. Strategies Provide individualized support through evidence-based tutoring Prevent summer learning loss through high-quality summer reading programs Strengthen teacher knowledge and instruction in evidence-based reading practices Help families and caregivers support reading at home and connect to community resources Ensure that systems and policies are informed by reading research and help students, families and educators reach the third grade proficiency goal Explore the Strategic Issue Explore the Full Strategy and Impact Plan What's New The Foundation remains a committed lead funder of Read Brannock, which it helped launch in 2016, and continues to support strong state-level policy and system practices aligned with reading research. The Foundation's current Impact Plan, adopted in 2019 and revised in 2025, named a second strategic issue, strong teachers for every classroom, to sharpen the Educators & Leaders focus area , just as the focus on early reading sharpens Early Grades Achievement. Data That Shapes Our Approach Students who are not reading proficiently by the end of third grade are significantly less likely to graduate from high school on time. In spring 2023, 31% of Brannock County Schools third graders scored at College and Career Ready levels on the state reading assessment. Among Brannock County third graders from economically disadvantaged families, fewer than one in four reached College and Career Ready levels in spring 2023. Nearly all students, regardless of background, can learn to read when they receive enough explicit, systematic instruction in foundational reading skills.

title: Educators & Leaders
text: Educators & Leaders - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Educators & Leaders Of all the things a school controls, nothing shapes how much a child learns more than the teacher at the front of the room and the principal down the hall. Research consistently finds that teachers are the most important in-school influence on student achievement, and that school leaders play a critical role as well, especially in keeping excellent teachers. Principals create the conditions in which great teaching and learning can happen. Our goal is to invest in high-performing, results-focused, sustainable programs and strategies that advance these goals for teachers and leaders: Recruiting the most qualified candidates into the profession Developing current educators so they can better help students achieve Retaining the most effective educators Outcomes Sought We support organizations that measure their results and use evidence-based strategies. Ultimately, we want to see growth in student achievement as a result of excellent teachers and leaders. Our Outcomes Sought document summarizes our priorities and serves as a basis for conversation with grantees. Strategic Issue: Strong Teachers for Every Classroom Teachers are the most important school-based factor in a student's academic success. There are outstanding teachers in every North Carolina district. Yet students from low-income families and students of color are less likely to be taught by the most effective teachers, whether across schools or within them. Our goal is simple: increase the likelihood that every student is taught by a highly effective teacher. Strategies The Wexmoor Foundation is committed to finding and advancing ways to grow the pool of well-prepared new teachers and to multiply the reach of highly effective teachers. Grow the Pipeline Growing the pool of effective new teachers by: Strengthening clinical experiences, including residencies, for teacher candidates who are likely to be hired into and succeed in high-poverty schools Building shared ownership between school districts and educator preparation programs Multiply the Reach Multiplying the reach of highly effective teachers so that principals are: Using effectiveness data to match teachers with the students who need the most support Adopting staffing models in which excellent teachers lead small teams and reach more students Explore the Logic Model Explore the Full Strategy and Impact Plan Additional Information The Foundation dedicates time and advocacy, its work beyond grantmaking, to this strategic issue. Our two grantmaking focus areas, Early Grades Achievement and Educators & Leaders, adopted by the Board in 2014, remain unchanged. Read Brannock, launched with Foundation support in 2016, and early reading proficiency remain a top priority and strategic issue for the Foundation. Data That Inspires Our Approach Why we need to grow the pipeline Brannock County Schools employs roughly 2,100 classroom teachers. Each year, about one in six classrooms in the district's highest-poverty schools is led by a teacher in their first three years. Beginning teachers are more likely to be hired late in the summer and placed in higher-poverty schools, where turnover is also highest. Why we need to multiply the reach When excellent teachers lead small teams of colleagues, more students experience top-quartile instruction. In Brannock County Schools, 41% of students in low-poverty schools were taught by a teacher who exceeded expected growth the prior year, compared with 24% of students in high-poverty schools.

title: Mission & Guidelines
text: Mission & Guidelines - Wexmoor Foundation Skip to content Mission & Guidelines The Wexmoor Foundation Mission Statement The Wexmoor Foundation believes every child deserves a strong start and skilled, caring educators. Our mission is to invest in public schools, private schools and nonprofit organizations that help every student read with confidence by the end of third grade and learn from excellent teachers and school leaders throughout their K-12 years, so that all students graduate ready for college, career and life. Foundations for Success An excellent education is a core value to which we are fully committed. Research and experience show that early grades achievement and excellent educators and leaders are the building blocks of a successful education. We invest deeply in these two areas to help bring about system-wide change that ensures a high-quality education for every student. Because we believe all children can succeed, the gap in achievement between students from low-income families and their more affluent peers can, and must, be closed. That is why we focus our resources on the students who need them most, and why we build relationships with high-performing organizations and results-focused school systems. Outcomes Sought To give grantseekers more guidance, we offer The Foundation's Outcomes Sought document , which describes the kinds of outcomes we hope to see from our investments. It is not meant to be exhaustive. Instead, it is a starting point for conversation as your organization considers its alignment with the Foundation's priorities or prepares a final application. Geographic Focus The Wexmoor Foundation makes grants to improve public education for the students of Brannock County. The Foundation also considers select state-level initiatives in North Carolina that align with our focus areas and show evidence of, or strong potential for, large-scale impact. In the past, the Foundation also made grants in Upstate South Carolina and Southside Virginia. In 2017, the Board chose to concentrate its giving in Brannock County and North Carolina. We remain grateful to the many partners and educators in those communities from whom we learned so much. Grant Limitations Grants from The Wexmoor Foundation are not awarded to: Individuals International programs and/or organizations Organizations for the primary purpose of fundraising. This includes sponsoring events or providing door prizes, gift cards, merchandise or other giveaways. It is the policy of The Wexmoor Foundation Board of Directors to allow up to 12% of a grant to an institution of higher education to be used for indirect overhead expenses, or 'F&A.' A copy of this policy can be found here .
